title: Mancini sets his sights on France after dominant victory over Turkiye
subtitle: Roberto Mancini claimed his first win since returning to manage Italy against Turkiye, but he is already thinking of the next match.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini immediately switched his focus to Italy's trip to France after he claimed his first win in his second stint with the Azzurri against Turkiye in the Nations League.
Mancini watched on as his Italy team emerged 4-1 victors in Bursaspor, with three goals inside the opening 27 minutes doing the damage against Vincenzo Montella's side.
Alessandro Bastoni handed the visitors a ninth-minute lead before Davide Frattesi rounded off an excellent passing move to double Italy's advantage in the 22nd minute.

Michael Kayode, on his international debut, put the Azzurri out of sight, as Italy scored three goals inside the first 30 minutes of play for the first time since a World Cup qualifier against Lithuania in September 2021.
Baris Alper Yilmaz threatened a comeback early in the second half, but Francesco Pio Esposito restored Italy's three-goal advantage in the 50th minute to seal an impressive win.
The result saw Italy win an away match by a 3+ goal margin for the first time since November 2019, when they beat Bosnia-Herzegovina 3-0.
More importantly, the Azzurri claimed their first win under Mancini, 1,198 days since his last win in charge of Italy, which came in a 3-2 triumph over the Netherlands in June 2023.

However, Mancini was already thinking about Italy's next game, which takes them to the Stade de France to face Zinedine Zidane's side, who sit top of Group A1 following their late win against Belgium on Monday.
"Now we have to focus on the next match, try to recover our strength, we've got fresh legs at home and will try to have our say in Paris," Mancini told RAI Sport.
The victory marked a huge improvement to the one Mancini oversaw on his second debut, with Italy outclassed during their 2-0 defeat against Belgium at the Stadio Olimpico.
Italy only registered an expected goals (xG) total of 1.7 from their 21 shots against Belgium, but they improved that to 2.4 from 14 attempts in a clinical display against Turkiye.

Mancini did, however, confirm that Giacomo Raspadori's substitution at half-time was because of an injury, and he was unable to add whether he would be available to face France and then Turkiye at home.
"We were on a pitch where it had been raining for a whole day, and it was only natural to expect a response from Turkiye," Mancini added.
"Everyone played a great game. Raspadori went off with a problem.
"We were worried that we might have to take him off after five minutes in the second half, so we substituted him at the break.
"The team pushed up, kept the ball, moved it around well. Raspadori did what we asked; he had a good game."
